must_ask_hmp: Monthly SF sales and rental starts/ends since August 2024 (vehicle units, battery-rental subscriptions, whole-vehicle rentals) - the only source for a real SF ramp curve.
Whether the >1,000 vehicles sold figure is SF-city-only or Bay Area/online, and how it reconciles with the '600+ e-mopeds in SF' quoted in press on 2026-04-02 with a '1,000 by end of year' target.

Customer geography: home zip/neighborhood and primary delivery zones of SF buyers/renters, to isolate the share attributable to the SoMa/Mission/Tenderloin/FiDi core zone (needed for the core-zone-to-core-zone ratio).

Legal/operational relationship between HMP Bikes (Davis, launched 2022) and '415 Ebikes' / Mandala Global, LLC (registered 2024-08-09) - owned store vs independent dealer - since it defines what 'replicating SF' in LA means.
Any SF activity before the 2024-08-09 business registration (pre-store sales, pop-ups) so the ramp clock starts at the right date.

Customer mix by platform (DoorDash / Uber Eats / Grubhub), full-time vs part-time, and language/community channels that drove adoption (word of mouth, WhatsApp/WeChat groups) - to judge LA transferability.
Battery-rental cohort data: when the 300+ battery renters signed up, churn, and how the June-2026 swap stations changed take-up.
Theft, repossession and non-payment rates for the ~100 vehicles on rent, and the SF store's fixed cost base (rent for 261 6th St) as the LA hub comparator.
surprises: The SF store ('415 Ebikes', Mandala Global, LLC) has a city business-registration start date of 2024-08-09, i.e., roughly 25 months of SF operation as of 2026-09-06 - a shorter history than a '>1,000 sold' installed base might suggest, which makes the SF ramp steep and the ramp curve for LA correspondingly short-horizon.

Press (Gazetteer SF, 2026-04-02) reported '600+ e-mopeds in SF' with a target of 1,000 by end of 2026; the CONTEXT states >1,000 already sold by 2026-09-06 - either ~400 units in five months or a definitional difference (sold vs on-street, SF vs Bay Area). Needs HMP reconciliation before the SF benchmark is fixed.
HMP is headquartered in Davis, CA (launched 2022), not San Francisco, and no 'HMP' DBA is registered in SF; the SF presence is a separately-named dealership entity.

SF is a national outlier for two-wheeled delivery: search snippets cite 72% of SF DoorDash deliveries on two wheels in 2025. A pure population/restaurant ratio LA-vs-SF will overstate LA unless the (unknown, likely far lower) LA two-wheel mode share is applied - this is a structural, not incidental, correction.

Battery-swap stations in SF only debuted in June 2026 (per press), so the 300+ battery-rental customers were acquired largely without swap infrastructure - the LA hub plan should not assume swap stations were a precondition for SF adoption.
